What is now genuinely grounded (verified, not assumed):
- Uniqueness of the candidate change: dep-5402 (v3.8.0, "Add in-memory template cache for email rendering", ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment) is the ONLY notification-service deployment in 2026-02-01..03-24, never rolled back [F1,F13], and the only other deployment anywhere is an unrelated auth-service jackson bump [F2]; the only config change anywhere is kafka retention [F3,F14], with 0 notification-service config changes.

Caveat properly recorded: 03-01..03-19 is unretained, so "first-ever" is bounded, not absolute.
- Shape: repeating ~20h ~48→~98% sawtooth, three cycles, reset on each OOM — not a minutes-scale replay spike [F9,F10]; the first two cycles precede the kafka maintenance entirely.
- Competing hypotheses contradicted, not merely untested: settlement-service (co-consumer of the same topics) has flat lag (window peak 82.06) in all three OOM buckets, zero restarts in 35 buckets, no memory sawtooth [F25,F26,F27]; kafka shows 0 under-replicated partitions in every bucket [F28]; order-service 0 restarts [F29]; no third consumer group is observable on any surface (kafka has no consumer_lag/consumer_groups; its logs carry no group ids) [F37-F42]. H1/H3/H4/H5 are each excluded by verified timing (cfg-2410 postdates restarts #1 and #2; a retention cut shrinks replay demand) or by absence of any provider-side evidence [F4,F12,F16].
- Directionality handled honestly: lag spikes sit in the same/adjacent buckets as the OOMs, and at 90-min granularity lag-precedes-OOM is only weakly supported [F30]. This is minor, not blocking: the once-daily ~20h cadence is incompatible with lag as the driver and consistent with restarts draining the group.

The one open hop — "cache entries accumulate without eviction" — is now known to be a CAPABILITY limitation, not a fixable request: no code/artifact retrieval exists (F19/F20/F22/F23/F24), confirmed redundantly. Absence of an eviction mention in a human-authored summary is not absence of a bound (F24), so I cannot claim the mechanism is proven; equally, no evidence contradicts it, and the bounded-cache alternative (H6) has no positive support — it exists only as the conditional residual to H2 (its own framing), and if H2's mechanism fails, H6 is a label for ignorance, not a competing explainer. Given zero contradicting findings for H2 and three independent confirmations of its timing (only notification-service change, ~23h pre-onset, per-day sawtooth), shipping H2 as "best-supported, mechanism assumed" is correct. Blocking the conclusion with "inconclusive" would add no information: no further tool call can separate H2 from H6, so the honest engineering action is to release with the assumption and caveat stated explicitly, and to note the one infra-side action that would close it (retrieve TemplateCache source).

Calibration: confidence is capped at 0.6, below the 0.6+ level a verified mechanism would justify; the label must remain "best supported" and NOT "proven", and the two residuals (unbounded-cache assumption; unretained 03-01..03-19 window) must ship with the RCA, not be dropped from it.

H2 is the best-supported hypothesis and its core chain is genuinely grounded: dep-5402 is the ONLY notification-service change in a wide window (F1/F13), it landed ~23h before the first OOM, memory shows a repeating ~20h sawtooth rather than a minutes-scale spike (F9/F10), and the competing Kafka/config/email theories are each contradicted by timing (F6/F14) or by the absence of any provider-side evidence (F4/F16). However, three gaps are blocking rather than cosmetic, and one is the difference between "H2 explains it" and "H2 is merely first among weak options":

(1) The leak MECHANISM is unverified. The stated causal hop "cache keys accumulate without eviction" rests on an assumption the analysts themselves flag — the change description says "cache" but never states eviction policy, TTL, or a size cap. If v3.8.0's TemplateCache is bounded/evicting, H2's mechanism collapses and we are back to an unexplained gradual ramp with no ranked cause. This is directly answerable via code/config and is the single highest-value query.

(2) Onset is never actually measured. All three restarts are within the observation window, and the "week-long, third this week" framing comes only from the reporter's narrative (explicitly logged as a gap). If restarts existed before 2026-03-21T00:00Z, H2 is rejected outright; if the first-ever restart is 03-21T22:59Z, H2 gains a clean onset. This is a binary test of the top hypothesis and is cheap to run.

(3) The shared-component alternative (H4/H5) was rejected on incomplete data: the settlement-service / other-consumer lag+restart comparison was never executed (budget exhaustion, per GAPS and T1's own note), and the Kafka upstream query failed. H4/H5 are currently dismissed largely because they are untested, which is not the same as contradicted — the "only notification-service changed" argument is strong but does not by itself exclude a cluster-side rebalance hitting one consumer's heap.

Temporal order and scope are otherwise sound, and the rejections of H1/H3/H4/H5 are each anchored in verified findings rather than in the reporter's opinion. One data-quality note: the lag spikes are confined to the OOM buckets, which is consistent with lag-as-consequence, but with 12h/2h bucketing a lag-PRECEDES-OOM ordering cannot be fully excluded, so the direction-of-causality hop should be held at moderate rather than high confidence.

critiques.summary:
Round 2 resolved 2 of my 3 blocking gaps and answered them as well as the toolset allows, but the single decisive gap remains open and is now known to be unanswerable within this evidence environment — yet H2's ranking still rests on it.

RESOLVED:
(1) Onset — F31/F32/F33/F34/F35/F36 answer the binary test. Within retained data (floor 2026-03-20T00:00Z) there are ZERO restarts before the 2026-03-21T00:00Z deploy, the first-ever OOMKilled is 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z (~23h post-deploy), and the restarts metric is 0.0 across all 289 points of 03-20. The onset is now measured, not narrated, and it is ~23h after dep-5402 and ~2.5d before cfg-2410. The honest caveat (retention floor means 03-01..03-19 cannot be excluded) is correctly recorded, not overclaimed.
(2) Shared-component alternative — F25/F26/F27/F28/F29 now genuinely CONTRADICT H4/H5 rather than merely leaving them untested: settlement-service, the co-consumer of the same topics, has flat lag (window peak 82.06) in all three OOM buckets, zero restarts in 35 buckets, and no memory sawtooth; kafka shows 0 under-replicated partitions in every bucket; order-service has 0 restarts. This is the direct disconfirmation round 1 asked for.

STILL OPEN / BLOCKING:
(3) H2's central mechanism — T4 confirmed twice over (F19/F20/F22/F23/F24, plus the explicit gap "no code-repository/artifact tool is available") that the eviction behavior of TemplateCache CANNOT be retrieved in this toolset. The single assumed hop — "cache entries accumulate without eviction, making memory grow monotonically with traffic" — is flagged by the automated check as the one hop with no evidence. This is not a request that failed for a fixable reason; it is a capability the environment does not have. That means no further query can close it, and it is exactly the difference between "H2's mechanism is established" and "H2 is first among weak options."

On the remaining calibration question: the lag-precedes-OOM direction (F30, gap on 90-min bucketing) stays weak, but this is genuinely minor — the once-daily ~20h sawtooth cadence (F8/F9/F10) is already incompatible with lag as the driver and consistent with restarts draining the group, so I do not treat this as blocking. Likewise, the possibility of an unlisted third consumer group (gap re: no kafka consumer_groups listing) is a residual worth one cheap check but does not, on its own, move the ranking given settlement-service's flat profile.

Net: H2 is the best-supported hypothesis and no competing hypothesis is now viable on the evidence. But its mechanism is unverifiable and H6 (unexplained gradual ramp) is explicitly constructed as the residual if that mechanism fails. I therefore cannot accept H2 as proven, and no additional tool call can make it provable. I am requesting one low-cost residual check on the only untested alternative channel, and capping confidence below the level that a verified mechanism would justify.

challenges.issue: The one non-evidenced hop ('cache entries accumulate without eviction, making memory grow monotonically with traffic') is the load-bearing link in the entire causal chain, and round 2 established it is UNVERIFIABLE in this environment (F20, F22, F23, F24; explicit gap: no code-repository/artifact tool, get_deployments/get_config_changes return metadata only; 0 notification-service config properties back the cache). The change description is human-authored summary text (F24), so 'no eviction mentioned' is not 'no eviction exists'. If TemplateCache is bounded/evicting, H2's mechanism collapses and H6 is promoted. This is a blocking epistemic gap, not a minor one.

Confidence 0.50 with a 0.60 cap is defensible only as 'best of a field where every alternative is contradicted'; it is NOT a 0.7-0.8 claim, because a single assumption carries the mechanism. The ranking is sound; the strength-of-proof language attached to it in the round-3 writeup must not drift upward. Do not let 'only remaining viable hypothesis' be restated as 'proven cause'.

Direction-of-causality hop (lag precedes OOM vs lag is a consequence of the down window) rests on 90-min bucketing, not the requested 2h/finer (F30, observability gap). Weak but non-fatal: the ~20h sawtooth cadence and post-restart lag normalisation (F11/F26) independently support lag-as-consequence. Should be held at moderate confidence, not used to strengthen H2.

H6 is a correct residual but should not be treated as a co-equal live hypothesis with H2 at 0.30 — it is the explicit fallback conditional on H2's mechanism being false, and no positive evidence supports it. Its 0.30 weight should be read as reflective of the unverified mechanism in H2, not as independent support for an unknown cause.

The residual untested channel: no kafka-level consumer_groups listing exists, so a third/unlisted consumer group on the identical topics cannot be checked (observability gap). Low expected value given settlement-service's flat lag/memory and 0 under-replicated partitions, but it is the only remaining channel through which a shared-Kafka story could survive, so it is worth the single cheap check.

critiques.summary:
Final round: H2 is the only viable hypothesis and the evidence, as far as this evidence environment permits, is as complete as it can get.

What is now genuinely grounded (verified, not assumed):
- Uniqueness of the candidate change: dep-5402 (v3.8.0, "Add in-memory template cache for email rendering", ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment) is the ONLY notification-service deployment in 2026-02-01..03-24, never rolled back [F1,F13], and the only other deployment anywhere is an unrelated auth-service jackson bump [F2]; the only config change anywhere is kafka retention [F3,F14], with 0 notification-service config changes.
- Onset measured, not narrated: retention floor is 2026-03-20T00:00Z [F34]; within it, restarts metric is 0.0 across 289 points of 03-20 and the 03-21T00:00 deploy bucket, and the first-ever OOMKilled (exit 137) is 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z, ~23h post-deploy and ~2.5d before cfg-2410 [F31,F32,F33,F35,F36]. Caveat properly recorded: 03-01..03-19 is unretained, so "first-ever" is bounded, not absolute.
- Shape: repeating ~20h ~48→~98% sawtooth, three cycles, reset on each OOM — not a minutes-scale replay spike [F9,F10]; the first two cycles precede the kafka maintenance entirely.
- Competing hypotheses contradicted, not merely untested: settlement-service (co-consumer of the same topics) has flat lag (window peak 82.06) in all three OOM buckets, zero restarts in 35 buckets, no memory sawtooth [F25,F26,F27]; kafka shows 0 under-replicated partitions in every bucket [F28]; order-service 0 restarts [F29]; no third consumer group is observable on any surface (kafka has no consumer_lag/consumer_groups; its logs carry no group ids) [F37-F42]. H1/H3/H4/H5 are each excluded by verified timing (cfg-2410 postdates restarts #1 and #2; a retention cut shrinks replay demand) or by absence of any provider-side evidence [F4,F12,F16].
- Directionality handled honestly: lag spikes sit in the same/adjacent buckets as the OOMs, and at 90-min granularity lag-precedes-OOM is only weakly supported [F30]. This is minor, not blocking: the once-daily ~20h cadence is incompatible with lag as the driver and consistent with restarts draining the group.

The one open hop — "cache entries accumulate without eviction" — is now known to be a CAPABILITY limitation, not a fixable request: no code/artifact retrieval exists (F19/F20/F22/F23/F24), confirmed redundantly. Absence of an eviction mention in a human-authored summary is not absence of a bound (F24), so I cannot claim the mechanism is proven; equally, no evidence contradicts it, and the bounded-cache alternative (H6) has no positive support — it exists only as the conditional residual to H2 (its own framing), and if H2's mechanism fails, H6 is a label for ignorance, not a competing explainer. Given zero contradicting findings for H2 and three independent confirmations of its timing (only notification-service change, ~23h pre-onset, per-day sawtooth), shipping H2 as "best-supported, mechanism assumed" is correct. Blocking the conclusion with "inconclusive" would add no information: no further tool call can separate H2 from H6, so the honest engineering action is to release with the assumption and caveat stated explicitly, and to note the one infra-side action that would close it (retrieve TemplateCache source).

Calibration: confidence is capped at 0.6, below the 0.6+ level a verified mechanism would justify; the label must remain "best supported" and NOT "proven", and the two residuals (unbounded-cache assumption; unretained 03-01..03-19 window) must ship with the RCA, not be dropped from it.

challenges.issue: The load-bearing hop — TemplateCache accumulates without eviction / lacks TTL or size cap — rests on zero evidence: the deployment record is human-authored summary text and no code/artifact retrieval exists (F19/F20/F22/F23/F24). Absence of an eviction mention is not evidence of absence of a bound. Also unresolved is whether insertion is on every render or on miss (F23). If the cache is in fact bounded, H2's mechanism collapses. Severity is downgraded only because no evidence contradicts it and the residual H6 has no independent support — but H2 must ship as 'mechanism assumed', never as proven.

Onset is bounded by a retention floor of 2026-03-20T00:00Z (F34). 'First-ever OOMKilled at 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z' is therefore a claim about the retained window only; restarts during 2026-03-01..03-19 can be neither confirmed nor excluded, and the report's 'third this week / week-long' framing remains unverifiable. A pre-existing ramp before the deploy would demote H2. This cannot be closed with any available tool, so it is a documented caveat rather than a blocking query.

H6 is the explicit residual conditional on H2's mechanism failing, not a co-equal live hypothesis, and it has no positive evidence (supporting F19/F20/F22/F23/F24 are all capability-absence findings). Its presence in the ranking reflects an unverified mechanism, not a competing cause; it should not be presented to stakeholders as an alternative explanation.

Rejection is well-grounded in verified co-consumer and cluster-health data (F25,F26,F27,F28,F29), but one channel remains structurally opaque: kafka exposes no consumer_groups/consumer_lag series and no group ids in logs (F37-F40), so an unlisted third consumer group on the same topics is untestable. This is a residual, not a blocker — a rebalance hitting only one consumer's heap while leaving the co-consumer and cluster signals untouched is already contradicted.

Direction-of-causality: at 90-min bucketing the lag spike cannot be shown to precede the OOM rather than accompany it (F30, bucketing gap). Mitigated by the ~20h sawtooth cadence, which is inconsistent with lag-driven memory growth and consistent with restarts draining the group; held at moderate, not high, confidence.
